cards.front: Recall a key point about The Economic Climate
cards.back: Interest rates set by the Bank of England affect borrowing costs: higher rates = more expensive loans and mortgages, reducing consumer spending and business investment.

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Economic Climate
cards.back: Inflation is the general rise in prices over time: high inflation erodes purchasing power and increases business costs, but low stable inflation (2% target) indicates a healthy economy.

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Economic Climate
cards.back: Exchange rates affect import/export prices: a stronger pound makes imports cheaper but exports more expensive, hurting UK exporters but helping importers.

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Economic Climate
cards.back: The business cycle has four stages: boom (high growth, low unemployment), recession (negative growth, rising unemployment), recovery (growth returns), and slowdown.

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Economic Climate
cards.back: Unemployment affects businesses: high unemployment reduces consumer spending power but makes it easier to recruit workers and may suppress wage demands.

cards.front: What should you know about business exam tips?
cards.back: When analysing economic impacts, use the CCE chain: Cause (the economic change) → Consequence (what happens in the economy) → Effect (how it impacts the specific business). Always specify which type of business is affected.

Students often make mistakes here. Wrong: A strong pound is always good for the UK economy. Correct: A strong pound helps importers (cheaper goods from abroad) and consumers (lower import prices), but hurts exporters (UK goods become expensive overseas) and UK manufacturers competing with cheap imports. cards.front: Assessment Objective Focus: The Economic Climate
cards.back: AO1 — Knowledge: Demonstrate knowledge of The Economic Climate with precise business/economic terminology. Define key terms and state accurate factual information.

cards.front: Understanding The Economic Climate in Business Context
cards.back: The Economic Climate is a key topic in GCSE Business Studies that affects how businesses operate in the UK economy. Understanding this concept requires knowledge of both theoretical principles and real-world application. The AQA specification requires you to explain, analyse and evaluate business concepts using appropriate terminology, and apply them to real business scenarios using UK examples.

cards.front: Applying The Economic Climate to UK Business Examples
cards.back: For the economic climate, applying theory to practice means using real UK business examples to illustrate your understanding. Small businesses face different challenges from large corporations when dealing with the economic climate. Consider how factors like business size, ownership structure, industry sector and market position affect the impact of the economic climate on a business.

cards.front: Exam Technique for The Economic Climate Questions
cards.back: GCSE Business exam questions about the economic climate range from 1-mark definition questions to 12-mark evaluation questions. For definition questions (1-2 marks), give a precise business definition. For explanation questions (3-4 marks), define and explain with a brief example.
